ground_truth_root_cause: The CDN origin shield (Fastly IAD shield node) lost connectivity to the frontend origin's AWS Network Load Balancer target group at 2026-05-07T07:22:58Z. The NLB target group 'frontend-tg' had all backend targets deregistered (healthy_targets=0), causing the origin shield to time out on every upstream request after ~9.2 seconds. Because the origin shield is the single upstream for all four CDN edge nodes (fra-01, sin-01, lax-01, ams-01), the timeout propagated globally: edges attempted direct-origin bypass but also failed via the same NLB, the shield circuit breaker opened, and CDN cache TTLs expired, resulting in 99% of user requests receiving 504 responses. The frontend service itself (all 8 pods) remained healthy throughout—internal p99 latency was 88ms and direct-origin requests succeeded—confirming the fault is entirely in the CDN/NLB layer, not in any application deploy.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately re-register healthy frontend backend instances into the NLB target group 'frontend-tg' in us-east-1 via the AWS console or CLI (aws elbv2 register-targets). 2. Confirm target group health checks pass (healthy_targets >= 2). 3. Force the Fastly IAD origin shield circuit breaker to reset by issuing a Fastly API purge-all or by temporarily toggling the shield off and back on via the Fastly control plane. 4. Verify CDN edge nodes resume cache fills and 504 rate drops to 0. 5. Conduct post-incident review to identify why all NLB targets were deregistered simultaneously (likely an erroneous auto-scaling event or manual deregistration) and add a guardrail to prevent target group from reaching 0 healthy targets.
